[SOURCE id=issue:cve-2026-41503:cve-2026-41503-summa:324815060097 kind=issue issue=2026 path=distilled_issue/1.BACnet-stack/#CVE-2026-41503.txt]
Issue: CVE-2026-41503
Summary: In bacnet-stack's `src/bacnet/rpm.c`, `rpm_decode_object_property()` in the ReadPropertyMultiple service decoder calls the deprecated `decode_tag_number_and_value()` before validating the buffer length. A truncated property list, such as a 1-byte property payload containing the extended tag marker `0xF9`, passes the context-specific tag check and then triggers a 1-byte out-of-bounds read inside `decode_tag_number()`, which reads `apdu[1]` without a length check. The issue affects deployments that enable the ReadPropertyMultiple confirmed service handler and was observed to cause crashes on embedded BACnet devices.
Reproduce: Build or run bacnet-stack with the ReadPropertyMultiple confirmed service handler enabled (enabled by default in the reference server). Compile the supplied PoC C program with AddressSanitizer, include `bacnet/rpm.h`, zero-initialize `BACNET_RPM_DATA`, and call `rpm_decode_object_property()` with a 1-byte APDU buffer containing `0xF9`. When the function processes that buffer, the context-specific check passes, `decode_tag_number_and_value()` is reached with no length parameter, and `decode_tag_number()` reads `apdu[1]` past the end of the 1-byte buffer. The expected result is an AddressSanitizer out-of-bounds read report or a crash.
[/SOURCE]

[SOURCE id=issue:cve-2026-41475:cve-2026-41475-summa:c7cf29fd27a9 kind=issue issue=2026 path=distilled_issue/1.BACnet-stack/#CVE-2026-41475.txt]
Issue: CVE-2026-41475
Summary: In bacnet-stack 1.5.0 development master at commit `578f507`, and according to the report all versions that use `wpm_decode_object_property()` with the deprecated decoder, `src/bacnet/wpm.c` uses `decode_tag_number_and_value()` from `src/bacnet/bacdcode.c` without checking that the current offset is still within `apdu_len`. The documented example is in `wpm_decode_object_property()`: after decoding tag 0 (property identifier), a 2-byte buffer leaves `len == 2`, and the next optional array-index parse calls `decode_tag_number_and_value(&apdu[2], ...)`. Because the deprecated decoder takes no buffer-length parameter and `decode_tag_number()` unconditionally reads `apdu[0]` and, for extended tags, `apdu[1]`, a truncated WritePropertyMultiple property payload causes a read past the end of the buffer. The report notes the same unchecked pattern at later calls in the same function. The demonstrated impact is an out-of-bounds read detected by AddressSanitizer; the report further states this may lead to crashes or information disclosure on affected embedded BACnet deployments.
Reproduce: Build a test program with AddressSanitizer that links against the bacnet-stack code and directly calls `wpm_decode_object_property()` from `bacnet/wpm.h`. Initialize a `BACNET_WRITE_PROPERTY_DATA` structure, then pass a 2-byte APDU buffer containing only context tag 0 and its property value: `0x09, 0x55`. In this input, decoding the property identifier consumes both bytes, so the next optional-tag parse in `wpm_decode_object_property()` calls `decode_tag_number_and_value(&apdu[2], ...)` on a pointer one byte past the end of the buffer. The expected result is an AddressSanitizer-detected out-of-bounds read during that second tag decode.
[/SOURCE]

[SOURCE id=issue:cve-2026-62973:cve-2026-62973-summa:7487fbadc732 kind=issue issue=2026 path=distilled_issue/1.BACnet-stack/#CVE-2026-62973.txt]
Issue: CVE-2026-62973
Summary: In bacnet-stack commit e2bdbf6, the official BACnet client application apps/readpropm is vulnerable while parsing ReadPropertyMultiple-ACK messages in bip_receive() -> npdu_handler() -> apdu_handler() -> My_Read_Property_Multiple_Ack_Handler() -> rpm_ack_decode_service_request(). A malicious BACnet/IP peer can answer a legitimate ReadPropertyMultiple request with a malformed but structurally valid ACK whose property-value [4] for start-time(142) contains a valid BACnetDateTime, then a semantically invalid application BOOLEAN, plus filler NULL tags. On failure, rpm_ack_decode_service_request() resets len to the full enclosed tag-4 payload length returned by bacnet_enclosed_data_length() instead of the remaining unconsumed length, advances apdu/apdu_len past the end of the global receive buffer Rx_Buf, and then calls bacnet_is_closing_tag_number() with the now-negative signed apdu_len, which is consumed as an unsigned size. The reproduced outcome is a global-buffer-overflow / out-of-bounds read on Rx_Buf; the source says the first invalid read is apdu[0] in bacnet_tag_number_decode(), and the verified impact is remote client-side denial of service.
Reproduce: 1) Use apps/readpropm from bacnet-stack commit e2bdbf6 as the client. 2) Start the Python 3 UDP PoC bound to 127.0.0.1:47808. 3) Have readpropm send a legitimate ReadPropertyMultiple request to that BACnet/IP peer. 4) When the PoC receives the request, copy request byte 8 as invoke_id and reply to the sender with a BVLC 0x81 0x0A frame whose NPDU/APDU prefix is 01 00 30 <invoke_id> 0E and whose body is a malformed but structurally valid ReadPropertyMultiple-ACK containing object-identifier device:123, list-of-results opening tag 1, propertyIdentifier start-time(142), and property-value
[/SOURCE]

[SOURCE id=issue:cve-2026-41502:cve-2026-41502-summa:c282c210e609 kind=issue issue=2026 path=distilled_issue/1.BACnet-stack/#CVE-2026-41502.txt]
Issue: CVE-2026-41502
Summary: No affected version is specified. In `bacnet-stack`, `src/bacnet/rpm.c` function `rpm_decode_object_id()` checks `apdu_len < 5` even though it then consumes 6 bytes: a context tag at `apdu[0]`, a 4-byte object identifier at `apdu[1..4]`, and an opening-tag check at `apdu[5]`. A truncated 5-byte ReadPropertyMultiple object-identifier buffer therefore passes validation and causes a 1-byte out-of-bounds read when `decode_is_opening_tag_number()` and `decode_tag_number()` read past the buffer end. The supplied PoC demonstrates this by directly calling `rpm_decode_object_id()` with a 5-byte APDU. The report says deployments with the ReadPropertyMultiple confirmed service handler enabled, which is enabled by default in the reference server, are affected and that the read can lead to crashes on embedded BACnet devices.
Reproduce: No build configuration or commands are provided. The document’s PoC (`poc_rpm_off_by_one.c`) reproduces the issue by: 1. Including `bacnet/rpm.h`, zeroing a `BACNET_RPM_DATA` structure, and creating a 5-byte `apdu` buffer containing `0x0C` followed by `0x00 0x00 0x00 0x01` (context tag 0 plus a 4-byte object identifier for analog-input instance 1). 2. Calling `rpm_decode_object_id(apdu, 5, &rpmdata)`. 3. Expected result from the report: the `apdu_len < 5` check accepts the 5-byte input, `decode_is_context_tag()` reads `apdu[0]`, `decode_object_id()` reads `apdu[1..4]`, and `decode_is_opening_tag_number(&apdu[5], 1)` then reads one byte past the end of the buffer via `decode_tag_number()`. The report states that, when reached through the ReadPropertyMultiple service handler, this out-of-bounds read can crash embedded BACnet devices.
[/SOURCE]
